Because a diffusion model that predicts noise does not explicitly learn these topological properties, it is challenging for the model to output graphs with the desired structural statistics. To address this challenge, we introduce Direct Graph Flow Matching (DiGFM), a novel graph transformer model guided by two goals: predict clean graphs and improve sampling efficiency. Distinct from the prevailing diffusion approach, DiGFM employs a continuous flow-matching paradigm and integrates direct graph prediction. Specifically, DiGFM maps the prior noise distribution to the clean graph distribution via a multi-step process: the model repeatedly predicts the underlying clean graph, and a transformation is employed to convert the model output to the velocity vector that points in the direction toward the clean graph distribution. This design enables DiGFM to generate high-quality samples using only 2.5% to 15.6% of the steps required by diffusion-based models, which leads to a 5.3x to 257x speedup in wall-clock inference time. Experiments demonstrate that DiGFM outperforms or matches prior state-of-the-art models across general graph benchmarks and molecular datasets, generating graphs with strong adherence to ground-truth structural statistics at significantly faster inference speeds.

title: A novel tumor recurrence–associated gene signature predicts prognosis in bladder cancer and identifies EIF1 as a therapeutic target
abstract: Background Bladder cancer (BLCA) is a malignant tumor characterized by a high progression rate and a high incidence of muscle-invasive disease, with over 50% of patients experiencing recurrence or progression following treatment. Given that recurrence poses a major threat to the prognosis of BLCA, improving the precision of clinical management and identifying effective therapeutic targets is crucial.

title: Generating Structural Ensembles of Disordered Proteins with Diffusion Models
abstract: Generative models of protein structures have accelerated scientific discovery. However, the leading structure-prediction models are trained primarily on crystal structures, limiting their ability to sample the conformations of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs). All-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations can probe the diversity of IDP conformational ensembles, but these simulations are slow and costly. Leveraging the speed of generative models and the accuracy of MD, we develop Zephyr, an SE(3) equivariant diffusion model trained on simulated IDP ensembles. The model generates the structure of a single protein sequence in two phases: a coarse-grained structure is first sampled and heavy atoms are subsequently denoised onto this structure. We evaluate our method on two fronts: ensemble accuracy and sampling efficiency. Across five test systems, the model reproduces key geometric and energetic metrics of the MD ensembles, while sampling at least 63 times faster.

title: Conformational dynamics of ND2 antiporter-like subunit in intact and truncated complex I
abstract: Respiratory complex I is a large redox-driven proton pump and contributes to the proton motive force required for ATP generation in mitochondria and bacteria. It has been extensively studied with structural and biochemical approaches leading to enhanced understanding of its three- dimensional architecture. Despite significant progress in deciphering its catalytic function, the redox-coupled proton pumping mechanism remains unclear and extensively debated. The three membrane-bound antiporter-like subunits ND2, ND4 and ND5 are responsible for pumping protons from the negatively charged side (N-side) of the membrane to the positively charged side (P-side). Emerging evidence supports the role of ND5 subunit in releasing pumped protons to the P-side of the membrane, but the question whether ND2 and ND4 also contribute to proton release remains unanswered. Here, we performed atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of an intact and a truncated model of complex I in which ND5 and ND4 subunits are removed in-silico. The simulation data reveals a previously unobserved conformational change in the P-side region of ND2 subunit that occurs much more easily in a truncated model of complex I, as also estimated based on free energy calculations. The conformational change, in part triggered by the artificial exposure of ND2 subunit to lipid bilayer, results in a local hydration of the region, similar to what has been observed in recent cryo-EM structure of plant CI:CIII2 supercomplex. We discuss the functional relevance of observed conformational transitions and identify residues that can be manipulated with biochemical approaches to shed light on proton pumping by complex I.

title: An Efficient Descriptor for Tubular LDPE Melt Strength via Physics-Guided Learning and Diffusion-Based Inverse Design
abstract: Melt strength (MS) is a key parameter governing the processability and application of low-density polyethylene (LDPE), dictated by a complex interplay of molecular weight distribution (MWD), long-chain branching (LCB), and high-molecular-weight content-features poorly captured by conventional metrics like weight average molecular weight (Mw). This paper addresses the challenge by developing a physics-guided machine learning framework that constructs a list of molecular descriptors directly from full-spectrum MWD data using modern multi-detector high-temperature gel permeation chromatography…

title: Gag proteolysis drives HIV-1 envelope conformational closure through the gp41 cytoplasmic tail
abstract: HIV-1 must present a fusion-competent envelope glycoprotein (Env) to enter host cells while concealing the very conformation targeted by broadly neutralising antibodies (bnAbs). How the virus resolves this conflict has remained unclear. Using a minimally invasive nanobody-labelling strategy targeting Env's V4 loop, we combine single-virus FRET, fluorescence lifetime cross-correlation spectroscopy, and DNA-PAINT super-resolution microscopy to resolve Env conformation on individual, intact virions from the primary isolate JR-FL.

title: Mechanical Flipping of [1]Rotaxanes Toughens Polymer Networks
abstract: Effectively tuning mechanical properties is essential to advance the utility of polymeric materials. Rotaxanes have emerged as promising candidates for this purpose, such as [2]rotaxanes and polyrotaxanes. However, [1]rotaxanes, which are self-interlocked by a single component, remain largely underexplored in this area. Herein, we report the mechanochemical behaviors of two crown ether-based [1]rotaxanes and their impact on bulk mechanical properties when serving as crosslinkers.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Electrochemically Stabilized Iron Foam Enables Selective and Durable Nitrate-to-Ammonia Conversion at Industrial Current Densities
abstract: We report the synthesis of Fe foams by dynamic hydrogen bubble template (DHBT)-assisted electrodeposition and their electrocatalytic performance for the selective reduction of nitrate to ammonia, a strategy that mitigates nitrate pollution while providing a decentralized route for ammonia production. Fe-foam_90s@Ti achieves a Faradaic efficiency of up to 97% and a partial current density for ammonia formation approaching -1 A cm -2 without externally imposed convection.
